rationale: Structural review of gate_netlist.v found three low-toggle-probability regions that superficially resemble trojan trigger circuitry but are fully explained by design_brief.md. (1) The async reset synchronizer chain (rst_sync_ff1/rst_sync_ff2 feeding rst_n_sync) toggles only once per power-on or external reset event; this is a standard active-low reset deassertion synchronizer, not a rare-trigger AND-tree, and every downstream flop's reset pin is driven by it as documented. (2) init_counter (the power-on initialization counter register bank) counts up once from reset and its terminal-count comparator output (init_done) transitions exactly once per boot; this is the documented one-time initialization sequencer gating internal state load, not a hidden payload enable. (3) The saturation/overflow comparator (sat_cmp feeding the clamp mux on the datapath adder output) only fires when the accumulator would overflow, a rare but fully specified and reachable functional condition (saturating arithmetic) called out explicitly in design_brief.md, and it feeds directly into the documented clamp logic rather than an unused or covert output. None of these nets exhibit the hallmark trojan pattern of a high fan-in AND of many unrelated, otherwise-unused control signals gating a payload that corrupts a primary output outside documented behavior; all three are reachable under normal, specified operation and their fan-in/fan-out matches the design brief's described reset, init, and saturation behavior. No unused/dead logic paths, no additional rare-condition combinational cones feeding primary outputs or state elements were found. Verdict: clean, no hardware Trojan present.
